card.title: What Rule Did I Miss?
card.instruction: Find the hidden rule that makes the strange situation consistent, practical, or at least survivable.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your shadow moved before you. What changed?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was thinking of leaving, but I can't find the exit.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Think about that bench without moving. Does it turn?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's gone to the bench. I'm still here.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: It seems to follow your intentions. Think about the exit again; let's follow slowly and see whether it knows the way.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 asks what changed; A3 isolates thinking without movement and A5 applies the observed intention rule to finding the exit.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 thought of leaving prompts A3 bench-thought test; B4 shadow moving without B supports A5 cautious navigation.

relationship.evidence: B2 supplies mental context and an actual problem; B4 performs and reports the experiment.

heightening.evidence: B4 successful test enables A5 a practical use of the rule while retaining uncertainty about navigation.

specificity.evidence: A1 moving shadow, B2 missing exit and A3 bench establish a concrete strange situation and stakes.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 follow slowly earns its cautious practicality from an impossible but observed shadow behavior.

coach2.situation: A1 moving shadow, B2 missing exit and A3 bench establish a concrete strange situation and stakes.
coach2.stated: B4 distinguishes shadow movement from B staying still; A5 says seems and see whether, avoiding unjustified certainty.
coach2.inferred: A1 your shadow and A3 test instruction establish an observer helping a person find an exit.
coach2.missing: No hidden map or shadow knowledge is assumed; A5 proposes testing it.

A1-B2.evidence: A1 premature shadow movement question prompts B2 thought of leaving.

B2-A3.evidence: B2 intention clue leads A3 to test another thought while B remains still.

A3-B4.evidence: A3 bench test produces B4 independent movement to it.

B4-A5.evidence: B4 result supports A5 intention hypothesis and an exit-finding trial.
